title: The Amulet of Samarkand
author: Jonathan Stroud
summary: Spirit hierarchies, character motivation, and the plot turns of Book 1. Twenty advanced questions.

verdicts.high: Exceptional. You could challenge a Marid.
verdicts.pass: Well done. A competent Djinni master.
verdicts.fail: Below the passing mark. No points awarded.

questions.q: What is Nathaniel's birth name, which he must keep secret to protect his identity?
questions.why: A magician's birth name is the one thing a spirit can use against them, which is why it is hidden from the moment of apprenticeship.

questions.q: Who is Nathaniel's official master in the magician's hierarchy?
questions.why: Underwood takes Nathaniel on as apprentice, though he badly underestimates him.

questions.q: What specific class of spirit is Bartimaeus?
questions.why: Bartimaeus is a djinni, the middle rank of the hierarchy, and is touchy about being mistaken for anything lower.

questions.q: Which human form does Bartimaeus most frequently favor when summoned?
questions.why: The form belongs to a magician Bartimaeus knew long ago, and he returns to it out of attachment rather than convenience.

questions.q: What is the primary reason Nathaniel illegally summons Bartimaeus?
options: To exact revenge on Simon Lovelace
questions.why: The summoning is personal. Lovelace humiliated Nathaniel publicly, and the theft is the opening move of his revenge.

questions.q: What is the primary magical function of the Amulet of Samarkand?
questions.why: Its defensive power is what makes it worth a coup: the wearer can stand inside an attack that would kill anyone else.

questions.q: Where does Simon Lovelace keep the Amulet hidden before it is stolen?
options: Inside a magical vault in Parliament
questions.why: Heddleham Hall is also where the conference is held, which is no coincidence.

questions.q: What is the name of Arthur Underwood's wife, who shows Nathaniel slight kindness?
questions.why: Martha's small kindnesses are the only warmth in the Underwood household, which sharpens what happens to her later.

questions.q: What object does Nathaniel use to spy on Bartimaeus while the djinni is away?
questions.why: The scrying glass holds a captive imp, and it is one of the first pieces of real magic Nathaniel builds himself.

questions.q: Who holds the position of Prime Minister of Britain during the events of the novel?
questions.why: Devereaux leads the magicians' government, which makes him the target of the plot at Heddleham Hall.

questions.q: Which mercenary entity is bound to Simon Lovelace and acts as his heavy enforcer?
questions.why: Jabor is relentless rather than clever, which is exactly why Bartimaeus has to outthink him instead of outfight him.

questions.q: Who is the Head of Internal Security for the magicians' government?
questions.why: Whitwell's position puts her at the centre of the investigation, and matters a great deal for Nathaniel's future.

questions.q: How does Nathaniel manage to learn advanced summoning magic at such a young age?
options: By reading Underwood's locked books in his study
questions.why: He teaches himself in secret from his master's own library, years ahead of what his lessons allow.

questions.q: In the spirit hierarchy, which of the following is considered the lowest and weakest form?
questions.why: The ranking runs upward from imps and mites through foliots and djinn to afrits and marids.

questions.q: How does Bartimaeus initially escape Lovelace's magical trap after stealing the amulet?
options: By shapeshifting into a bird and flying out a window
questions.why: Shapeshifting is his standard escape, and the bird form is small enough to take an exit a person could not.

questions.q: Who tragically perishes when Lovelace's spirits attack the Underwood household?
questions.why: Both Underwoods die, and Nathaniel's part in bringing that on the house is the turning point of his character.

questions.q: At what major event is Lovelace planning to use the Amulet to stage a coup?
options: The Magicians' Conference at Heddleham Hall
questions.why: The conference puts the entire government in one room, which is the point of holding it at his own estate.

questions.q: What is the name of the resistance group made up of non-magical commoners?
questions.why: The Resistance is made up of commoners with a natural resilience to magic, and grows in importance across the series.

questions.q: What new, official 'master name' does Nathaniel adopt at the end of the book?
questions.why: Taking the name John Mandrake closes the book on the boy and opens it on the government magician he becomes.

questions.q: What is the ultimate leverage that can break a magician's control over a summoned spirit?
options: Knowing the magician's true birth name
questions.why: Knowing the birth name reverses the balance of power entirely, which is why the secret is guarded so fiercely.
